title: CISA added CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to the KEV catalog on 26 October 2026 (due 29 October): the first KEV listing of the two PHP flaws
note: For the journalist, the correspondent and the cyber desk. CISA's KEV catalog, version 2026.10.26, released 22:24 UTC on 26 October: both CVEs added on 26 October, due date 29 October, known ransomware use 'Unknown'; the alert is dated 26 October 2026 (cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/26/cisa-adds-two-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog). The editor spotted it on 27 October. Our captures of 26 October (the last at 17:03 UTC) did not have it; the catalog and the alert were captured at 00:45 UTC on 27 October (watch vault 7r83qic5: us/registry/cisa-kev/cisa-kev-json and us/registry/cisa-kev/cisa-alert-2026-10-26-adds-two-kev); the series kev-listed reads 2 (was 0); the ledger record is-it-exploited has a fourth statement. A KEV entry means CISA holds evidence of exploitation and names no victim, so it does not by itself end the statement on /compromise/ (no named organisation has confirmed a compromise through php2shell); it changes the answer to 'is it exploited'. The pages that say 'neither CVE is in the KEV catalog' (state of affairs, the desk's numbers) need the date of this change.
